entries.q: What are your hours?
entries.a: Monday: closed. Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday and Sunday: 10 AM to 6 PM. Friday and Saturday: 10 AM to 8 PM. All times are Central. Holiday hours may vary.

entries.q: Are your hours different on holidays?
entries.a: The site says holiday hours may vary. News is posted on Facebook, Instagram and TikTok, or you can call or text 715-628-0468 to check before you come.

entries.q: Where is the shop?
entries.a: The Blessed Fig Tree is at 800 5th Ave, Antigo, WI 54409, in downtown Antigo, at Fifth Avenue and Clermont Street. It's in the former Buckalows Eatery building, and the public library is directly across the street.

entries.q: Where do I park?
entries.a: Curb parking in front of the building is limited to 2 hours. For longer visits, use the Guest Parking lot across the street: walk up the Clermont St sidewalk and cross 5th Ave, and the shop is right there. The Find us section has a map of the route.

entries.q: Can I park overnight?
entries.a: The site sends longer visits to the Guest Parking lot across the street, and its photo of the lot across the street calls it the overnight lot. To confirm overnight parking for your visit or stay, email owner@theblessedfigtree.com or call or text 715-628-0468.

entries.q: How do I contact the shop?
entries.a: Email owner@theblessedfigtree.com, or call or text 715-628-0468. The shop is at 800 5th Ave, Antigo, WI 54409.

entries.q: Are you on social media?
entries.a: Yes. News and events are posted on Facebook (blessedfigtree), Instagram (blessedfig) and TikTok (blessedfigtree).

entries.q: Do you have events or book clubs?
entries.a: News and events are posted on the shop's Facebook, Instagram and TikTok. The website doesn't list a book club or event schedule, so for current events ask the shop: email owner@theblessedfigtree.com or call or text 715-628-0468.

entries.q: What do you sell?
entries.a: About 4,000 personally selected books, mostly new with some used. The main sections are manga, fantasy, history and philosophy, Wisconsin and the outdoors, and games and puzzles, including books for tabletop roleplaying games. There are also imported chips, candy and drinks, work by local artists, and figures, statues and gifts.

entries.q: Do you have used books?
entries.a: Yes, some. The shop's roughly 4,000 books are mostly new, with some used books mixed in.

entries.q: Do you buy or trade used books?
entries.a: The website doesn't say whether the shop buys used books or takes trade-ins. Ask the shop before you bring a box in: email owner@theblessedfigtree.com or call or text 715-628-0468.

entries.q: Can you order a book you don't have?
entries.a: The website doesn't describe special orders. Ask the shop and they can tell you: email owner@theblessedfigtree.com or call or text 715-628-0468.

entries.q: Do you have a certain book in stock?
entries.a: The website doesn't list the shop's stock, so the quickest way to check for a particular book is to call or text 715-628-0468 or email owner@theblessedfigtree.com.

entries.q: Do you have manga?
entries.a: Yes. Manga fills a long wall and is the section the shop is best known for, with collectible figures along the top shelves. The shop counts it among the best manga selections in northern Wisconsin.

entries.q: Do you have fantasy books?
entries.a: Yes. Fantasy fills two full bookcases, with wizard-themed gifts and a few dragons keeping watch.

entries.q: Do you have history and philosophy books?
entries.a: Yes. History and philosophy is one of the main sections: nonfiction for long Northwoods winters, from the past to the big questions. There's also a section of books about Wisconsin, the Northwoods and the outdoors.

entries.q: Do you have D&D or tabletop RPG books?
entries.a: Yes. There's a section of books for tabletop roleplaying games, for players and for the people who run them, alongside puzzles and other games.

entries.q: Do you sell snacks and drinks?
entries.a: Yes. The shop carries imported chips, candy and drinks.

entries.q: Do you serve tea or coffee?
entries.a: The website lists imported snacks and drinks on the shelves but doesn't mention tea or coffee. Ask the shop what's on hand: email owner@theblessedfigtree.com or call or text 715-628-0468.

entries.q: Do you sell art and gifts?
entries.a: Yes. Alongside the books are works by local artists, figures and statues worth a second look and wizard-themed gifts.

entries.q: Do you sell gift cards?
entries.a: The website doesn't mention gift cards. Ask the shop: email owner@theblessedfigtree.com or call or text 715-628-0468.

entries.q: What payment do you take?
entries.a: The website doesn't list payment methods. Ask the shop: email owner@theblessedfigtree.com or call or text 715-628-0468.

entries.q: What are your prices?
entries.a: The website doesn't list prices. Ask the shop about a particular book or item: email owner@theblessedfigtree.com or call or text 715-628-0468.

entries.q: Is the shop wheelchair accessible?
entries.a: The website doesn't describe accessibility at the shop. Ask before you visit and the shop can tell you: email owner@theblessedfigtree.com or call or text 715-628-0468.

entries.q: Can I bring my dog?
entries.a: The website doesn't say whether pets are allowed in the shop. Ask first: email owner@theblessedfigtree.com or call or text 715-628-0468.

entries.q: Is there a place for kids?
entries.a: Yes. Der Kinderwald (the Child's Forest) is the secret reading nook tucked inside the shop: a woodland hideaway with a little wooden door, built for kids and anyone young at heart. Bring a book from the shelves and settle in.

entries.q: Can I get a book recommendation?
entries.a: Yes. The owner runs the shop and is usually downstairs during business hours. Ask for a recommendation.

entries.q: When did the shop open?
entries.a: The Blessed Fig Tree opened in downtown Antigo in May 2023, in the former Buckalows Eatery at 800 Fifth Avenue.

entries.q: What do reviewers say about the shop?
entries.a: The shop shows a 4.9-star rating from 69 Google reviews, and the home page quotes a selection of them, with a link to read them all on Google.

entries.q: Can I stay upstairs?
entries.a: Yes. The shop rents furnished apartments with full kitchens in the same building: the 3-Bed Reading Apartment and the 1-Bedroom Downtown, for a weekend, a work trip or a month. You can see them and request a stay at stays.theblessedfigtree.com.

entries.q: What are check-in and check-out times?
entries.a: Check-in for the apartments upstairs is at 3:00 PM, and check-out is by 11:00 AM.

entries.q: What is there to do in Antigo?
entries.a: The home page's Explore Antigo section covers downtown (boutiques, cafés, antiques, the Dixie Lunch and Yesterday's Sign Park), the public library across the street, the Springbrook Trail with its disc golf course, the Ice Age Trail, the Langlade County Historical Society Museum, and the county's lakes, trout streams and ski trails.

entries.q: Who is Goose Goose?
entries.a: Goose Goose is the shop's concrete porch goose: guardian of the porch, star of the shop's videos and survivor of the basement. He changes forms with the seasons. His page also has a sourced encyclopedia of geese and a quiz.

entries.q: What is the Manga Worldview Guide?
entries.a: It's a guide for parents of every background, still in beta. For each English-licensed manga it describes what the story holds up as a good life, in neutral words, then grades it S to F from the point of view of the tradition you choose. You can also set the reader's age, browse popular series, search all manga with filters, or take a short family values quiz.

entries.q: How does the manga guide grade books?
entries.a: Each series is read from inside each tradition using that tradition's own teaching, then graded on its message: S Excellent fit (affirms core values), A Strong fit (a few small concerns), B Good with talk (some things to discuss), C Mixed (real concerns alongside good themes), D Serious concerns (many would wait or read together), F Conflicts (at odds with core teaching throughout). A grade isn't lowered just because a series is intense. What's shown on the page is rated separately as a depiction concern: Minor, Discuss or Significant. A grade with a dashed border is provisional.

entries.q: Which traditions or religions does the manga guide cover?
entries.a: You pick the tradition under "Grades for". The choices include Techno-Puritan (the starting choice), Christian (any), Catholic, Baptist, Non-denominational Evangelical, Pentecostal / Charismatic, Eastern Orthodox, Orthodox Jewish, Muslim, Conservative / traditional and Secular progressive, among others. The description of each series is the same for every reader; your tradition only changes the grade and the order. Each tradition's standard is written out under How we grade, and Philosophies explained describes every tradition in plain words.

entries.q: What age is a manga right for?
entries.a: Each graded series gets a suggested age band of 7+, 10+, 13+, 16+ or 18+, worked out from its mature content scores (a series fits a band only if every category is at or under that band's limit). It's the guide's suggestion, not the publisher's rating, and where available the publisher's own rating is shown beside it. Set the reader's age on the guide's start page to see popular series suited to that age.

entries.q: What does the mature content score mean?
entries.a: It answers one question: how much mature content is on the page, from 0 (none) to 10 (extreme). It's scored separately for violence, fear and intensity, sexuality and romance, language, substances, mental health and self-harm, imitable behavior and commercialism, and the headline number is the highest of those. It doesn't say whether the story approves of what it shows; the S to F grade covers the message.

entries.q: Where does the manga guide's information come from?
entries.a: From AniList, MangaUpdates, MangaDex, Wikipedia, publisher pages, parent guides and reviews. Fan wikis are used for plot facts only, and the guide never uses pirated scans or fan translations. Each entry is labeled Not analyzed yet, From summaries (built from synopses, ratings and reviews, no pages read) or Full read (checked against the official English edition and signed off by a reviewer). The tradition guides are still drafts being checked against their sources.

entries.q: Is there a quiz to match manga to my family's values?
entries.a: Yes. "Our family's values" is a 2-minute quiz on everyday values like honor and tradition, and the "In-depth family profile" is a longer quiz across every category for a closely matched list. Both are under Explore in the manga guide.

entries.q: What is the Antigo Almanac?
entries.a: The Antigo Almanac gives Antigo's year in real numbers: when people come, what they do and where money moves. It has 24 entries in four parts (the year in Antigo, including weather and daylight; visitors; the town; and land and history, including the woods and lakes, how Antigo began and its library), and every entry names its source. The numbers describe the country, state, county or region, never a single business, and it isn't financial advice.

entries.q: What's happening in Antigo this season?
entries.a: The Antigo Almanac's seasons pages list the town's year: winter trails and events, spring fishing and the Off-Road National, summer farmers market, Fourth of July and County Fair, and the fall hunting seasons and downtown holiday run, each with its source. For events at the shop itself, follow its Facebook, Instagram or TikTok.

entries.q: What is The Unwritten?
entries.a: The Unwritten is a free pixel-art adventure in the style of 1990s role-playing games, set in the real streets of Antigo. You start at the shop at 800 5th Ave, walk downtown and step into the places you know. It plays in your browser with nothing to install and no account.

entries.q: Is the game finished?
entries.a: No. It's a huge work in progress: an early, unfinished build. Expect rough edges, placeholder lines, missing story and things that change from week to week. Much of the town and most of the story are still being built.

entries.q: How do I play The Unwritten?
entries.a: Open the game page and choose NEW GAME, then pick who you are, a name, the story setting and how to play. On a keyboard: arrow keys (or W A S D) to walk, A (Enter or Z) to look and talk, hold B (X or Esc) to run, M for the map, and C to save. It's best on a computer with a keyboard.

entries.q: Where is my game save kept?
entries.a: Your save stays on your own device, in the browser you play in. Save from the menu (press C, or the SAVE button on a phone), then choose CONTINUE on the title screen next time. Because the save lives in that browser, it won't follow you to another device or browser, and clearing your browser's site data erases it.

entries.q: Can I play the game on my phone?
entries.a: Yes. On a touch screen the game shows an on-screen pad: a D-pad on the left, A and B buttons on the right (hold B to run), and MAP and SAVE buttons in the middle. The game is best on a computer with a keyboard.

entries.q: Is the game OK for kids?
entries.a: When you start a new game you choose the story setting. Standard is for teens and up: the real town, told honestly, with a lighter hand. Mature hits harder, with horror, drinking, grief and faith argued hard and no padding, but it is never sexual.

entries.q: Can I run the bookstore in the game?
entries.a: Yes. When you start a new game, set PLAY to BOOKSTORE to run The Blessed Fig Tree: order books, buy used boxes, plan events, then open up and ring up customers. Rent is due every Monday. Set PLAY to ADVENTURE to walk the real town of Antigo instead. The game's ALMANAC menu holds the same almanac as the website, with its pages hidden around town.

entries.q: Is there a guide or walkthrough for The Unwritten?
entries.a: Yes. The game guide covers controls on keyboard and phone, saving, battles, a cheat sheet, a step-by-step walkthrough of the current build, the places in town and the party.
